page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin beside the italic quotation. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: ram tuam maxillam, obverte ei & alteram. &c. Respondeo, hunc esse sensum ejus loci, potius, quam injuste quis velit vindicare injuriam sibi illatam, malit eam omnino non vindicari. Idque quo magis in nobis illa vindictæ cupido, quæ exorbitat, reprimatur, ac coerceatur, non ut legitimus defensionis modus auferatur. Unde eleganter ad hunc locum respiciens Augustinus, sic scripsit.

p.i: Ea quæ in novo testamento à san-ctis facta sunt, valent ad exempla intelligendarum scripturarum, quæ in præceptis digesta sunt. Velut cum legimus in Evangelio: Accepisti alapam, para alteram maxillam. Exemplum autem patientiæ nullum, quam ipsius Domini excellentius invenimus, & ipse cum alapâ percussus esset, non ait: Ecce alteram maxillam, sed ait: si male dixi, exprobra de malo: si autem bene, quid me cædis? page.notes: Marginal notes are in the right margin: "Auguft. libr.1. de Mendac." beside the first line of the quotation, and "Et deScr-mon. do-mini in mont.lib. 1.c.37." beside "alapâ". The word "legimus" has a blot over it that may hide a letter. The reference marks in the text are not clearly visible. The running head is printed as "De Duéllis." in the scan; I have read it as "De Duellis." The page number is printed as "141" (possibly "14I"). The word "sanctis" at the line break is partly obscured and read from context.
